--- /dev/null
+++ b/bandit/core/nosec.py
@@ -0,0 +1,281 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+"""Selector expressions and statement-scoped suppression directives."""
+
+import bisect
+import fnmatch
+import re
+import tokenize
+
+from bandit.core import extension_loader
+
+DIRECTIVE = re.compile(r"#\s*nosec-(begin|end|next-line)\b(.*)", re.IGNORECASE)
+SELECTOR_TOKEN = re.compile(r"[\w*]+|[|&!(),\-]|[^\s,]")
+IGNORED = {
+    tokenize.ENCODING,
+    tokenize.COMMENT,
+    tokenize.NL,
+    tokenize.INDENT,
+    tokenize.DEDENT,
+    tokenize.ENDMARKER,
+}
+GROUPING = {"(", ")", "[", "]", "{", "}", ";", "..."}
+
+
+def merge(*suppressions):
+    """Union legacy suppression values: None is absent, set() is blanket."""
+    result = None
+    for suppression in suppressions:
+        if suppression is not None:
+            if not suppression:
+                return set()
+            if result is None:
+                result = set()
+            result.update(suppression)
+    return result
+
+
+class Selector:
+    """Resolve selectors against the enabled finding IDs.
+
+    Precedence, highest first: !, & and -, then explicit/implicit union.
+    Empty resolved sets mean no suppression, unlike legacy nosec values.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self, enabled):
+        self.enabled = set(enabled)
+
+    def atom(self, token):
+        if token.lower() == "all":
+            return self.enabled.copy()
+        if token.lower() == "none":
+            return set()
+        if token.upper().startswith("B"):
+            matches = {
+                test
+                for test in self.enabled
+                if fnmatch.fnmatchcase(test, token.upper())
+            }
+            if matches:
+                return matches
+        test = extension_loader.MANAGER.get_test_id(token)
+        return {test} & self.enabled if test else set()
+
+    def parse(self, expression):
+        if not expression.strip(" ,\t\r\n"):
+            return set()
+        matches = list(SELECTOR_TOKEN.finditer(expression))
+        tokens = [match.group() for match in matches]
+        position = 0
+
+        def primary():
+            nonlocal position
+            if position >= len(tokens):
+                raise ValueError("missing operand")
+            token = tokens[position]
+            position += 1
+            if token == "!":
+                return self.enabled - primary()
+            if token == "(":
+                value = union()
+                if position >= len(tokens) or tokens[position] != ")":
+                    raise ValueError("unclosed group")
+                position += 1
+                return value
+            if not re.fullmatch(r"[\w*]+", token):
+                raise ValueError("invalid operand")
+            return self.atom(token)
+
+        def intersection():
+            nonlocal position
+            value = primary()
+            while position < len(tokens) and tokens[position] in {"&", "-"}:
+                operator = tokens[position]
+                position += 1
+                right = primary()
+                value = value & right if operator == "&" else value - right
+            return value
+
+        def union():
+            nonlocal position
+            value = intersection()
+            while position < len(tokens) and tokens[position] != ")":
+                if tokens[position] in {"|", ","}:
+                    position += 1
+                else:
+                    left = matches[position - 1].end()
+                    right = matches[position].start()
+                    if not expression[left:right].isspace():
+                        raise ValueError("missing union separator")
+                value |= intersection()
+            return value
+
+        try:
+            resolved = union()
+            if position != len(tokens):
+                raise ValueError("unexpected closing group")
+        except (ValueError, RecursionError):
+            resolved = set()
+            for token in re.split(r"[\s,]+", expression):
+                resolved.update(self.atom(token))
+        if not resolved:
+            return None
+        return set() if resolved == self.enabled else resolved
+
+
+class Suppressions(dict):
+    """Inline line map plus directives indexed by logical statement.
+
+    Token spans keep a suppression on a compound statement's header separate
+    from its suite, and let a marker on any continuation line cover the whole
+    statement, including AST children whose own ranges are shorter.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self, tokens, enabled, parse_inline, lines):
+        super().__init__()
+        selector = Selector(enabled)
+        directives = {}
+        statements = []
+        current = []
+        depth = 0
+        for token in tokens:
+            lineno = token.start[0]
+            if token.type == tokenize.COMMENT:
+                match = DIRECTIVE.search(token.string)
+                if match:
+                    kind, argument = match.groups()
+                    kind = kind.lower()
+                    directives[lineno] = (
+                        kind,
+                        None if kind == "end" else selector.parse(argument),
+                    )
+                else:
+                    self[lineno] = parse_inline(token.string)
+            if token.type in IGNORED:
+                continue
+            if token.type == tokenize.NEWLINE or (
+                token.string == ";" and depth == 0
+            ):
+                if current:
+                    statements.append(current)
+                    current = []
+                continue
+            current.append(token)
+            if token.type == tokenize.OP:
+                if token.string in {"(", "[", "{"}:
+                    depth += 1
+                elif token.string in {")", "]", "}"}:
+                    depth -= 1
+        if current:
+            statements.append(current)
+
+        # Decorators belong to the following definition, rather than consuming
+        # a next-statement directive on their own.
+        decorated = []
+        decorators = []
+        for statement in statements:
+            if statement[0].string == "@":
+                decorators.extend(statement)
+            else:
+                decorated.append(decorators + statement)
+                decorators = []
+        if decorators:
+            decorated.append(decorators)
+        statements = decorated
+
+        # Explicitly paired regions may span indentation changes. Unclosed
+        # indented regions fall back to the physical indentation boundary.
+        explicit = set()
+        pending = []
+        for lineno, (kind, _) in directives.items():
+            if kind == "begin":
+                pending.append(lineno)
+            elif kind == "end" and pending:
+                explicit.add(pending.pop())
+
+        # Even a `none` region occupies a slot on the nesting stack.
+        regions = {}
+        stack = []
+        for lineno, line in enumerate(lines, 1):
+            indentation = len(line) - len(line.lstrip(b" \t\f"))
+            stack = [
+                entry
+                for entry in stack
+                if not entry[0] or indentation >= entry[0]
+            ]
+            kind, suppression = directives.get(lineno, (None, None))
+            if kind == "end" and stack:
+                stack.pop()
+            regions[lineno] = merge(*(entry[1] for entry in stack))
+            if kind == "begin":
+                stack.append(
+                    (0 if lineno in explicit else indentation, suppression)
+                )
+
+        encoding = tokens[0].string if tokens else "utf-8"
+        decoded = [line.decode(encoding, errors="replace") for line in lines]
+        if decoded:
+            decoded[0] = decoded[0].lstrip("\ufeff")
+
+        def ast_position(position):
+            # tokenize columns count characters; AST columns count UTF-8 bytes,
+            # even when the source file uses a different encoding.
+            row, column = position
+            return row, len(decoded[row - 1][:column].encode("utf-8"))
+
+        self.starts = [ast_position(s[0].start) for s in statements]
+        self.ends = [ast_position(s[-1].end) for s in statements]
+        self.regions = regions
+        self.suppressions = [
+            merge(
+                *(
+                    merge(regions.get(line), self.get(line))
+                    for line in range(start[0], end[0] + 1)
+                )
+            )
+            for start, end in zip(self.starts, self.ends)
+        ]
+        # Punctuation-only and ellipsis-only lines never consume a next marker.
+        eligible = []
+        for index, statement in enumerate(statements):
+            for token in statement:
+                if token.string not in GROUPING:
+                    eligible.append((token.start[0], index))
+                    break
+        eligible.sort()
+        for lineno, (kind, suppression) in directives.items():
+            if kind == "next-line":
+                target = bisect.bisect_right(
+                    eligible, (lineno, len(statements))
+                )
+                if target < len(eligible):
+                    index = eligible[target][1]
+                    self.suppressions[index] = merge(
+                        self.suppressions[index], suppression
+                    )
+        # Combining specific directives may itself resolve to blanket.
+        self.enabled = set(enabled)
+
+    def for_context(self, context, result=None):
+        positions = [(context.get("lineno", 0), context.get("col_offset", 0))]
+        if (
+            result is not None
+            and result.lineno is not None
+            and (
+                result.lineno != context.get("lineno")
+                or result.col_offset >= 0
+            )
+        ):
+            positions.append((result.lineno, max(result.col_offset, 0)))
+        values = []
+        for position in positions:
+            # File-level plugins may report a comment without an AST node.
+            values.append(self.regions.get(position[0]))
+            index = bisect.bisect_right(self.starts, position) - 1
+            if index >= 0 and position <= self.ends[index]:
+                values.append(self.suppressions[index])
+        return merge(*values)
+
+    def normalize(self, suppression):
+        if suppression and self.enabled and suppression >= self.enabled:
+            return set()
+        return suppression

index 185d6ae..d3e1de0 100644

   assert yaml.load("{}") == []  # nosec assert_used
 
+Regions and the next statement
+~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
+
+Use ``# nosec-begin`` and ``# nosec-end`` to suppress a region, or
+``# nosec-next-line`` to suppress the next statement. Directive keywords are
+case-insensitive. Selectors follow the keyword directly, without a prefix:
+
+.. code-block:: python
+
+  # nosec-begin B602, B607
+  subprocess.Popen('/bin/ls *', shell=True)
+  subprocess.Popen('/bin/echo hello', shell=True)
+  # nosec-end
+
+  # nosec-next-line subprocess_popen_with_shell_equals_true
+  # Comments and blank lines do not consume the directive.
+  subprocess.Popen('/bin/echo hello', shell=True)
+
+A region starts on the physical line after its begin directive and ends before
+the line containing its end directive. Regions may nest; an end closes the most
+recent active region. Extra text after an end is ignored, as are unmatched ends.
+An unclosed region runs to the end of the file, except that an indented unclosed
+region ends at a later line with less leading whitespace. This uses the line's
+indentation, even when the directive follows code on that line.
+
+The next-statement directive skips blank lines, comment-only lines, and lines
+containing only grouping punctuation, semicolons, or ellipsis literals. A
+multiline statement is suppressed as a whole if any of its lines is suppressed,
+even when a region ends inside that statement. A begin directive never applies
+to preceding statements. Multiple applicable suppressions are combined, and a
+blanket suppression takes precedence over specific tests.
+
+Region and next-statement selectors support:
+
+* An omitted or empty selector, or ``all``, for all enabled tests.
+* ``none`` for no suppression.
+* Test IDs, full test names, and ID prefix globs such as ``B60*``.
+* Spaces, commas, or ``|`` for union, ``&`` for intersection, ``-`` for
+  difference, and ``!`` for negation relative to the enabled test set.
+* Parentheses for grouping. Negation binds first, then intersection and
+  difference (left to right), then union.
+
+For example, ``# nosec-next-line (B60* | B101) - B607`` suppresses matching
+enabled tests except B607. If an expression cannot be parsed, its whitespace-
+and comma-separated tokens are treated as a plain union instead. An expression
+resolving to an empty set has no effect. A resolved blanket suppression
+increments the ``nosec`` metric; a non-empty specific suppression increments
+``skipped_tests`` for each suppressed finding.
+
+``--ignore-nosec`` disables inline, region, and next-statement suppressions.
+
 -----------------
 Scanning Behavior
 -----------------

@@ -0,0 +1,431 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+
+import io
+import textwrap
+import unittest
+
+from bandit.core import config
+from bandit.core import manager
+
+
+class NosecDirectiveTests(unittest.TestCase):
+    def scan(self, source, ignore_nosec=False, profile=None):
+        scanner = manager.BanditManager(
+            config.BanditConfig(),
+            "file",
+            debug=True,
+            ignore_nosec=ignore_nosec,
+            profile=profile,
+        )
+        # Debug traversal otherwise writes to BanditMetaAst's class-level map.
+        scanner.b_ma.nodes = {}
+        scanner._parse_file(
+            "directives.py", io.BytesIO(textwrap.dedent(source).encode()), []
+        )
+        self.assertEqual([], scanner.skipped)
+        findings = [(item.test_id, item.lineno) for item in scanner.results]
+        metrics = scanner.metrics.data["directives.py"]
+        return findings, (metrics["nosec"], metrics["skipped_tests"])
+
+    def test_region_boundaries_and_case(self):
+        findings, metrics = self.scan(
+            """\
+            assert True  # NoSeC-BeGiN B101
+            assert True
+            assert True  # NOSEC-END ignored B101
+            assert True
+        """
+        )
+        self.assertEqual([("B101", 1), ("B101", 3), ("B101", 4)], findings)
+        self.assertEqual((0, 1), metrics)
+
+    def test_nested_regions_union_and_pop(self):
+        findings, metrics = self.scan(
+            """\
+            # nosec-begin B101
+            # nosec-begin B102
+            assert True
+            exec('x = 1')
+            # nosec-end
+            exec('x = 1')
+            assert True
+            # nosec-end
+            assert True
+        """
+        )
+        self.assertEqual([("B102", 6), ("B101", 9)], findings)
+        self.assertEqual((0, 3), metrics)
+
+    def test_blanket_nested_with_specific(self):
+        for outer, inner in [("", "B101"), ("B101", "all")]:
+            with self.subTest(outer=outer, inner=inner):
+                findings, metrics = self.scan(
+                    f"# nosec-begin {outer}\n# nosec-begin {inner}\n"
+                    "assert True\nexec('x = 1')\n"
+                )
+                self.assertEqual([], findings)
+                self.assertEqual((2, 0), metrics)
+
+    def test_none_still_nests_without_overriding_outer(self):
+        findings, metrics = self.scan(
+            """\
+            # nosec-begin B101
+            # nosec-begin none
+            assert True
+            # nosec-end
+            assert True
+            # nosec-end
+            assert True
+        """
+        )
+        self.assertEqual([("B101", 7)], findings)
+        self.assertEqual((0, 2), metrics)
+
+    def test_unmatched_end_and_unterminated_region(self):
+        findings, metrics = self.scan(
+            """\
+            # nosec-end
+            assert True
+            # nosec-begin
+            assert True
+        """
+        )
+        self.assertEqual([("B101", 2)], findings)
+        self.assertEqual((1, 0), metrics)
+
+    def test_auto_dedent_uses_leading_whitespace(self):
+        findings, metrics = self.scan(
+            """\
+            def example():
+                value = 1  # nosec-begin B101
+                assert value
+            assert True
+        """
+        )
+        self.assertEqual([("B101", 4)], findings)
+        self.assertEqual((0, 1), metrics)
+
+    def test_nested_auto_dedent_preserves_outer(self):
+        findings, metrics = self.scan(
+            """\
+            # nosec-begin B101
+            def example():
+                # nosec-begin B102
+                exec('x = 1')
+            exec('x = 1')
+            assert True
+        """
+        )
+        self.assertEqual([("B102", 5)], findings)
+        self.assertEqual((0, 2), metrics)
+
+    def test_explicit_region_can_cross_dedent(self):
+        findings, metrics = self.scan(
+            """\
+            def example():
+                # nosec-begin B101
+                assert True
+            assert True
+            # nosec-end
+            assert True
+        """
+        )
+        self.assertEqual([("B101", 6)], findings)
+        self.assertEqual((0, 2), metrics)
+
+    def test_begin_is_not_retroactive_to_compound_header(self):
+        findings, metrics = self.scan(
+            """\
+            def example(password='secret'):
+                # nosec-begin
+                assert True
+        """
+        )
+        self.assertEqual([("B107", 1)], findings)
+        self.assertEqual((1, 0), metrics)
+
+    def test_multiline_end_does_not_restore_statement(self):
+        findings, metrics = self.scan(
+            """\
+            # nosec-begin B102
+            exec(
+                # nosec-end
+                'x = 1'
+            )
+            exec('x = 1')
+        """
+        )
+        self.assertEqual([("B102", 6)], findings)
+        self.assertEqual((0, 1), metrics)
+
+    def test_begin_within_statement_applies_to_later_lines(self):
+        findings, metrics = self.scan(
+            """\
+            exec(  # nosec-begin B102
+                'x = 1'
+            )
+            # nosec-end
+            exec('x = 1')
+        """
+        )
+        self.assertEqual([("B102", 5)], findings)
+        self.assertEqual((0, 1), metrics)
+
+    def test_suppresses_children_across_whole_statement(self):
+        findings, metrics = self.scan(
+            """\
+            values = [
+                exec('x = 1'),
+                # nosec-begin B102
+                0,
+                # nosec-end
+            ]
+        """
+        )
+        self.assertEqual([], findings)
+        self.assertEqual((0, 1), metrics)
+
+    def test_next_skips_comments_blanks_grouping_and_ellipsis(self):
+        findings, metrics = self.scan(
+            """\
+            # NoSeC-NeXt-LiNe B102
+
+            # explanation
+            (); []; {}; ...;
+            (
+                exec(
+                    'x = 1'
+                )
+            )
+            exec('x = 1')
+        """
+        )
+        self.assertEqual([("B102", 10)], findings)
+        self.assertEqual((0, 1), metrics)
+
+    def test_next_only_one_statement_on_semicolon_line(self):
+        findings, metrics = self.scan(
+            "# nosec-next-line B101\nassert True; assert True\n"
+        )
+        self.assertEqual([("B101", 2)], findings)
+        self.assertEqual((0, 1), metrics)
+
+    def test_next_after_inline_directive(self):
+        findings, metrics = self.scan(
+            "assert True  # nosec-next-line\nassert True\nassert True\n"
+        )
+        self.assertEqual([("B101", 1), ("B101", 3)], findings)
+        self.assertEqual((1, 0), metrics)
+
+    def test_stacked_next_and_region_and_inline_union(self):
+        findings, metrics = self.scan(
+            """\
+            # nosec-begin B101
+            # nosec-next-line B102
+            # nosec-next-line B307
+            assert exec('x = 1') or eval('1')  # nosec B104
+        """
+        )
+        self.assertEqual([], findings)
+        self.assertEqual((0, 3), metrics)
+
+    def test_inline_blanket_dominates_specific_directive(self):
+        findings, metrics = self.scan(
+            """\
+            # nosec-next-line B101

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+
+import unittest
+
+from bandit.core import nosec
+from bandit.core import utils
+
+
+class SelectorTests(unittest.TestCase):
+    def test_selectors(self):
+        selector = nosec.Selector({"B101", "B102", "B602", "B607"})
+        cases = [
+            ("", set()),
+            (" , \t", set()),
+            ("all", set()),
+            ("none", None),
+            ("ALL - none", set()),
+            ("B101", {"B101"}),
+            ("assert_used", {"B101"}),
+            ("b60*", {"B602", "B607"}),
+            ("B101, exec_used B602", {"B101", "B102", "B602"}),
+            ("B101 | B102", {"B101", "B102"}),
+            ("B10* & B101", {"B101"}),
+            ("B10* - B101", {"B102"}),
+            ("!B10*", {"B602", "B607"}),
+            ("!(B101 | B102)", {"B602", "B607"}),
+            ("B101 | B102 & B602", {"B101"}),
+            ("(B101 | B102) & B602", None),
+            ("(B10* | B60*) - (B102 | B607)", {"B101", "B602"}),
+            ("all - B101", {"B102", "B602", "B607"}),
+            ("all & B101", {"B101"}),
+            ("none | B101", {"B101"}),
+            ("B101 - B101", None),
+            ("B999", None),
+            ("unknown_name", None),
+            ("B101 |", {"B101"}),
+            ("B101 &", {"B101"}),
+            ("B101, ( B102", {"B101", "B102"}),
+            ("B101, & B102", {"B101", "B102"}),
+            ("B101!B102", None),
+            ("B101(B102)", None),
+            ("(B101) (B102)", {"B101", "B102"}),
+            ("B101 ) B602", {"B101", "B602"}),
+            ("all &", set()),
+            ("none &", None),
+        ]
+        for expression, expected in cases:
+            with self.subTest(expression=expression):
+                self.assertEqual(expected, selector.parse(expression))
+
+    def test_enabled_universe(self):
+        selector = nosec.Selector({"B101", "B102"})
+        self.assertEqual({"B102"}, selector.parse("!B101"))
+        self.assertEqual(set(), selector.parse("B10*"))
+        self.assertEqual(set(), selector.parse("B101 | B102"))
+        self.assertIsNone(selector.parse("B602"))
+        self.assertIsNone(selector.parse("!all"))
+
+    def test_blacklist_name(self):
+        self.assertEqual(
+            {"B307"}, nosec.Selector({"B101", "B307"}).parse("eval")
+        )
+
+    def test_deep_invalid_expression_falls_back(self):
+        self.assertEqual(
+            {"B101"},
+            nosec.Selector({"B101", "B102"}).parse("( " * 2000 + "B101"),
+        )
+
+    def test_union_all_context_lines(self):
+        context = {"linerange": [1, 2, 3]}
+        self.assertEqual(
+            {"B101", "B102"},
+            utils.get_nosec({1: {"B101"}, 3: {"B102"}}, context),
+        )
+        self.assertEqual(
+            set(), utils.get_nosec({1: {"B101"}, 3: set()}, context)
+        )
+        self.assertIsNone(utils.get_nosec({}, context))
+
+    def test_blanket_dominates(self):
+        self.assertEqual(set(), nosec.merge({"B101"}, set(), {"B102"}))
+        self.assertEqual(set(), nosec.merge(set(), {"B101"}))
+        self.assertIsNone(nosec.merge(None, None))
